prompt: Create a sprite design comparison sheet translating the reference two cage-abdomen spiders into actual retro 2D side-scrolling game pixel-art style. Six isolated full-body sprites in evenly spaced 3 columns x 2 rows on solid dark desaturated teal background. Top row SKULL version, bottom row DOLL version, no text anywhere. Columns: ceiling idle, ceiling crawling with alternating leg positions, silk-hauling pose with forelegs reaching down. Same scale and anatomy in every cell, clear 24pixel margins, no overlapping cells. Strong crisp deliberate pixel clusters and limited palette, NOT realistic illustration, NOT blurry downsampled concept art. Each creature should look like roughly 160x180 native pixel sprite enlarged nearest neighbor 3x for inspection. Near-black chitin with restrained bluegray edge highlights, eight hooked angular legs, tiny pale spider eyes, large upright hollow organic cage abdomen. All creatures face right in three-quarter SIDE view suitable for platform game. Top: three pale adult human skulls visibly nestled behind widely spaced black chitin cage ribs. Bottom: three obviously artificial porcelain baby doll heads, cracked surfaces, painted cheeks, glass eyes and unsettling expressions, behind same ribs. Pale contents must be large enough to distinguish at gameplay size. Keep abdomen cage organically connected to spider thorax, not separate hanging cage. Four legs visibly hook at a consistent ceiling plane per row, no rendered ceiling or environment. Hauling pose uses two bent limbs gripping short taut silk strand, long world tether not baked in. No prey or cocoon, no gore, no gradients outside sprites, no labels or UI. Faithful identity to reference but simplify hairs/detail for clean readable sprite silhouettes. These are six pose studies, not a finished animation.
status: Visual pose studies only; not registered, extracted or animation-tested production sprites
